2.1 Depending on the method of heat transfer, taking place from gas, the recuperator can be grouped into following three categories:

a) Convection type - The tubular heat transferring element may be made either from drawn tubes, ERW tubes, fin or fabricated or from cast tubes. Material of construction for the cast tubes could be either alloy cast iron or alloy steel, depending on the design requirement. ,4 convection type tubular recuperator may be installed .in the flue duct. has two concentric shall with the air/gas to b) Radiation type - Radiation type recuperator be preheated passing through the annular space between the two shells and the hot waste gases passing in the centre. This is called a #Double Shell Type' radiation recuperator. If tubes are arranged around the rising/descending hot waste gases, it is called a #Tube Radiation Recuperator.' c) Combination recuperator - AS the name suggests, generally a part of it is a radiation recuperator ( either double shell or tubular type ) and the other part is a convection There could be also combination of a double shell radiation recuperator and recuperator. a tubular radiation recuperator. 2.2 Selection The following guidelines are recommended:

2.2.1 Convection type recuperators are generally used with flue gas temperatures below 1 050�C at recuperator. For higher flue gas temperature, radiation type recuperators are used. In special applications, recuperators achieving heat transfer, both by radiation and convection methods, are also used. Recuperators can be categorized depending on the constructional features and the method in which it is installed on the path of the waste gases. 2.2.2 Metallic recuperators can be installed with furnaces, using various types of fuels like coal, ci\ and gases either by themselves or in combination with other. The specification of fuel that is intended to be used in. the furnace shall be taken into consideration while selecting the type of It is also Important to consider the corrosion aspect of the fuel/flue gases while recuperator. Only that fuel, for which selecting the material for CcnStrUCtiOn Of the heat exchanging surfaces. the furnace equipped with a recuperator has been designed, shall be used. ln case of any change in type or quality of fuel in such a furnace, a prior consultation with the furnace/recuper_ ator manufacturer is necessary. 3. 3.2.1 Performance guaran!ee by the manufacturer - It should be understood that the salient performance data for the recuperator, such as air preheat temperature, overall calorific efficiency and the pressure drops on the waste gas and air/fuel gas side would be attainable so far as the input data regarding the operation of the furnace/process equipment given by the purchaser are the same in actual operation and this would be guaranteed by the manufacturers.
4. Material

for Recuperator

4.1 The manufacturer of recuperators normally designs the recuperator. and guarantee its performance and the suitability of materials used for construction to the purchaser. Therefore, it is the responsibility of the manufacturer to satisfy'himself that the right quality of materials have been chosen and used in manufacturing the recuperator to achieve the guaranteed performance
for the recuperator. The materials used should withstand the wall temperatures which is attain-

able in the heat transfer areas at the maximum operating conditions as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser, Conditions as dictated by presence of undesirable impurities in

7. Workmanship

and Finish

7.1 The workmanship SO far as bending, welding of pressure parts and the general appearance are concerned, should be checked to ensure that the recuperators are clean, sound and free from harmful defects. 8. Repair 8.1 In case a recuperator does not give satisfactory result when put to pressure test, rectification of the same is allowed twice by the same method as employed for the manufacture of the recuperator. Therefore, the recuperator would be put to pressure test again. 9. Certificate 9.1 The manufacturer b) Warranty shall furnish certificates to the purchaser in respect of the folIowing:

a) Result of pressure test, and on workmanship and use of proper material.

6.2 In addition to the above, if specifically agreed between the purchaser and manufacturer, a certificate giving the specifications of the materials used and a copy of the.original manufacturers' certificate for the same, may be furnished to the purchaser. 9 10.1 Running Tests - Testing of recuperators in operation would mean investigation in continuous operation along with related furnace when fully stabilized under specified operating conditions. 3 10. Testing of Recuperator While in Operation

The period of test should be chosen in such a way that related furnace is in the same thermal The running tests should consist of: state at the start and end of the test. a) Preheat test for air/gas, and b) Pressure drop test: 1) Air side, and 2) Gas side ( flue gas ). 10.1.1 A test programme should be drawn jointly by the contracting parties ( purchaser and supplier ) mentioning the measurements to be taken, allowable tolerance, and measuring and regulating equipment/instrumentS to be used. 10.1.2 The time schedule for conducting performance tests should be mutually agreed upon. Tests should be conducted not earlier than three weeks and not later than 12 weeks after the date of final commissioning/commercial use. 10.1.3 Tests should be performed by the supplier in the presence of client's accredited representative. A record should be kept through the test recording all readings at short intervals of about 15 minutes on indicating/measuring instruments. 10.2 Preheat Test - Preheat temperature of gas/air should be measured by inserting a thermocouple at a point in the delivery pipline within one metre from the preheated gas/air outlet of the recuperator and connected to a calibrated temperature measuring instrument. Simultan ously, the measurement of the flue gas temperature and cross checking by way of calculatin$ 7 based on the rate of fuel usage and oxygen content in the flue gas during test period ), to volume of flue gases and gas/air being preheated are also necessary to co-relate with the preheat value. 10.3 Pressure Drop Test - The tolerance in the guarantee value under specified flow conditions shall be mutually agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. Testing under steady flow conditions should be carried out with calibrated pressure gauge to simultaneously measure pressure accross the recuperator both on flue gas side and on gas/air side. The locations of pressure taps must conform to relevant norms prescribed by the instrument maker. 10.4 When the related furnace will often run on also based on a partial load. The value of,the in recuperator performance should be mutually specified in the test programme. The results of contracting parties. partial loads, performance test can be conducted partial load and corresponding guarantee values agreed to between the contracting parties and the corresponding tests should be signed by the

EXPLANATORY

NOTE

Recuperators, in general, and metallic recuperators, in particular are being increasingly used' in industrial furnaces in India. At present, the manufacture and te&ing of metallic recuperators is being done according to the standard of the manufacturers in the country, In order to provide some guidelines for metallic recuperators, this code has been prepared. The aim of the standard is to - draw up specification for recuperators which would help, both, the purchaser and the manufacturer in ordering and manufacturing of a metallic recuperators, and the requirements to be met by the manufacturer. It also covers the provisions of the guarantee 9 that the manufacturer is expected to give for the recuperators. 4
Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
